meta.chapterLabel: Lesson 14: Giving and Receiving: I Received It from My Friend (Extras)

items.english: Sweatshirt
items.target: トレーナー
items.note: Built in Japan out of English, but it does NOT mean 'trainer'. Not a person who trains you, and not British 'trainers' (shoes) — it's a crewneck sweatshirt.
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-3) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Clothing and accessories, Lesson 14's field (earrings, necklace, blouse, tie)

items.english: Smith-san gave his wife a ring.
items.target: スミスさんはおくさんにゆびわをあげました
items.note: With あげます the に marks the person who RECEIVES, and を marks the thing that changes hands.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: particle).

items.english: Nakamura-san lent her scarf to Emma-san.
items.target: なかむらさんはエマさんにスカーフをかしました
items.note: With かします the に marks the person who gets the loan.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (chapter material the base extraction missed). Lifted VERBATIM from TARGET DIALOGUE (closing summary line).

items.english: My wife received some earrings from Nakamura-san.
items.target: つまはなかむらさんにイヤリングをもらいました
items.note: The same event as なかむらさんはつまにイヤリングをくれました, told from the receiver's side. くれます puts the giver first; もらいます puts the receiver first and marks the giver with に.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: kuremasu).

items.english: Lisa-san gave me some chocolate for Valentine's Day.
items.target: リサさんはバレンタインデーにわたしにチョコレートをくれました
items.note: Two に doing different jobs: the first marks the occasion, the second marks the receiver. A receiver of わたし forces くれました over あげました.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: kuremasu).

items.english: I get a sweater from my mother for my birthday.
items.target: わたしはたんじょうびにははにセーターをもらいます
items.note: Present-tense もらいます for a regular, repeated event. The に after はは still marks the giver, exactly as it does in the past tense.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: paradigm).

items.english: Smith-san's wife received a ring from him.
items.target: おくさんはスミスさんにゆびわをもらいました
items.note: Minimal pair with スミスさんはおくさんにゆびわをあげました. The identical に marks the RECEIVER with あげます but the GIVER with もらいます: the verb, not the particle, tells you which way the ring travelled.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: particle).

items.english: Oh, I have a scarf.
items.target: あ、スカーフがありますよ
items.note: The chapter's first use of あります as "have": the thing owned takes が, not を. よ flags it as news to the listener.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (chapter material the base extraction missed). Lifted VERBATIM from TARGET DIALOGUE.

items.english: Emma-san gave me a concert ticket.
items.target: エマさんはわたしにコンサートのチケットをくれました
items.note: くれました, not あげました. The test is simple: if わたし is the one receiving, the verb has to be くれます.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: kuremasu).

items.english: Emma-san is going to borrow a car from Nakamura-san tomorrow.
items.target: エマさんはあしたなかむらさんにくるまをかります
items.note: Mirror of なかむらさんはあしたエマさんにくるまをかします. Only the two names and the verb swap; everything else in the frame holds still.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: paradigm).

items.english: It's a lovely bag, isn't it? Where did you buy it?
items.target: すてきなバッグですね。どこでかいましたか
items.scene: complimenting something a friend is carrying
items.note: The natural follow-up to a compliment. どこで, not どこに: で marks the place where an action happens.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: vocabulary).

items.english: Nakamura-san didn't lend Emma-san any money.
items.target: なかむらさんはエマさんにおかねをかしませんでした
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: paradigm).

items.english: Here, please take this.
items.target: これ、どうぞ
items.note: Said while holding the thing out. はい、どうぞ (Lesson 4) is the general "here you go"; これ、どうぞ points at the specific item.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (chapter material the base extraction missed). Lifted VERBATIM from TARGET DIALOGUE.

items.english: I'm very sorry.
items.target: どうもすみませんでした
items.scene: apologizing again for something you just did
items.note: どうも intensifies the apology; the past form すみませんでした is for something already done.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (chapter material the base extraction missed). Lifted VERBATIM from SPEAKING PRACTICE 1.

items.english: Why is that?
items.target: どうしてですか
items.note: Answered with から (kara), the 'because' particle this lesson teaches.
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: the question どうして (dōshite) asks, placed here because this is the lesson that teaches how to answer it.

items.english: Hoodie
items.target: パーカー
items.note: Another English-looking word that shifted meaning: not an English 'parka' (a heavy winter coat) but a hooded sweatshirt.
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-3) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Clothing and accessories, Lesson 14's field (earrings, necklace, blouse, tie)

items.english: Hat
items.target: ぼうし
items.note: Covers hats and caps alike. Note the long vowel: ぼう (bō), not ぼ.
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-3) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Clothing and accessories, Lesson 14's field (earrings, necklace, blouse, tie)

items.english: What did Smith-san receive for his birthday?
items.target: スミスさんはたんじょうびになにをもらいましたか
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (chapter material the base extraction missed). Lifted VERBATIM from EXERCISES: Listen and answer (1).

items.english: I have a car.
items.target: わたしはくるまがあります
items.note: The same あります you learned for "there is", but with a person as the topic it means "have". わたしは names the owner and くるまが the thing owned.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: arimasu-have).

items.english: This hat is cute.
items.target: このぼうしはかわいいです
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-3) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Clothing and accessories, Lesson 14's field (earrings, necklace, blouse, tie)

items.english: Nakamura-san gave my wife some earrings.
items.target: なかむらさんはつまにイヤリングをくれました
items.note: くれます covers the speaker's whole side, not only the speaker. A gift to my wife, my family or my colleague still counts as coming towards me, so it is くれました and not あげました.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: kuremasu).

items.english: I don't have any money.
items.target: わたしはおかねがありません
items.note: The thing you have (or lack) takes が, never を: おかねをありません is wrong.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: arimasu-have).

items.english: Who did he receive it from?
items.target: だれにもらいましたか
items.scene: asking a follow-up question about a gift someone has just mentioned
items.note: だれに, not だれから — with もらいます the giver is marked by に.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (chapter material the base extraction missed). Lifted VERBATIM from EXERCISES: Listen and answer (2).

items.english: I didn't have any plans yesterday.
items.target: わたしはきのうよていがありませんでした
items.note: よていがありません is how you say you're free. Note ありませんでした, not じゃありませんでした: this is the verb あります, not です.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: arimasu-have).

items.english: Why
items.target: どうして
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-2) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: doushite becomes answerable once Lesson 14 teaches kara (because)

items.english: Smith-san didn't give Lisa-san any chocolate.
items.target: スミスさんはリサさんにチョコレートをあげませんでした
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: paradigm).

items.english: Belt
items.target: ベルト
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-3) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Clothing and accessories, Lesson 14's field (earrings, necklace, blouse, tie)

items.english: Nakamura-san has an appointment this evening.
items.target: なかむらさんはこんばんやくそくがあります
items.note: やくそくがあります is the normal way to say you're already booked. The time word sits between the topic and the thing you have, with no particle of its own.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: arimasu-have).

items.english: Emma-san bought a new blouse at a department store yesterday.
items.target: エマさんはきのうデパートであたらしいブラウスをかいました
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: vocabulary).

items.english: Smith-san has time the day after tomorrow afternoon.
items.target: スミスさんはあさってのごごじかんがあります
items.note: じかんが あります is how you say "have time / be free".
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (chapter material the base extraction missed). Adapted from EXERCISES: State someone's schedule.

items.english: Nakamura-san has a concert ticket.
items.target: なかむらさんはコンサートのチケットがあります
items.note: Watch the particle swap on one and the same noun: with あげます/もらいます the ticket takes を (チケットをもらいました), but with あります in the "have" sense it takes が.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: particle).

items.english: I'm going to give my wife a necklace for our wedding anniversary.
items.target: わたしはけっこんきねんびにつまにネックレスをあげます
items.note: あげます is correct here because the necklace leaves the speaker. Present-tense ます also covers a plan for the future.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: paradigm).

items.english: It's a lovely scarf, isn't it?
items.target: すてきなスカーフですね
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (chapter material the base extraction missed). Lifted VERBATIM from TARGET DIALOGUE.

items.english: Yes, I'm fine.
items.target: ええ、だいじょうぶです
items.scene: answering だいじょうぶですか (daijōbu desu ka, "are you all right?") after someone bumps into you
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (chapter material the base extraction missed). Lifted VERBATIM from SPEAKING PRACTICE 1.

items.english: Nakamura-san is going to lend Emma-san her car tomorrow.
items.target: なかむらさんはあしたエマさんにくるまをかします
items.note: The lend/borrow pair in the present. Compare エマさんはあしたなかむらさんにくるまをかります, which is this same event from the borrower's side.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: paradigm).

items.english: These are black socks.
items.target: これはくろいくつしたです
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-3) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Clothing and accessories, Lesson 14's field (earrings, necklace, blouse, tie)

items.english: Do you have time tomorrow evening?
items.target: あしたのよるじかんがありますか
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (chapter material the base extraction missed). Adapted from SPEAKING PRACTICE.

items.english: Smith-san had a business trip last week.
items.target: スミスさんはせんしゅうしゅっちょうがありました
items.note: "Have" in the past is ありました. The thing had keeps が in every tense.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: arimasu-have).

items.english: Nakamura-san gave me some flowers.
items.target: なかむらさんはわたしにはなをくれました
items.note: Minimal pair with わたしはなかむらさんにはなをあげました. Same event shape, opposite direction. Because the flowers come TO me, Japanese swaps the verb: なかむらさんはわたしにはなをあげました is wrong, and it is the classic beginner mistake here.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: kuremasu).

items.english: Smith-san is going to give his colleagues a Kyoto souvenir tomorrow.
items.target: スミスさんはあしたどうりょうにきょうとのおみやげをあげます
items.note: Same frame as あげました but in the present, which reads as a future plan.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: paradigm).

items.english: I gave Nakamura-san some flowers.
items.target: わたしはなかむらさんにはなをあげました
items.note: あげます is the verb for a thing moving AWAY from the speaker. The に marks the person who received it. Flip the direction, make わたし the receiver, and あげます becomes impossible; that case needs くれます.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: kuremasu).

items.english: My father gives me money for my birthday.
items.target: ちちはたんじょうびにわたしにおかねをくれます
items.note: Plain present くれます for something that happens every year. The direction rule does not depend on tense: the money comes to me, so あげます is still impossible.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: kuremasu).

items.english: It's a bit cold, isn't it?
items.target: ちょっとさむいですね
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (chapter material the base extraction missed). Lifted VERBATIM from TARGET DIALOGUE.

items.english: This is a black belt.
items.target: これはくろいベルトです
items.note: くろい (kuroi) is a true い-adjective, so の never appears here. Same for あかい (akai), あおい (aoi) and しろい (shiroi) — those four and no others.

items.target: くつした
items.note: くつ (kutsu) 'shoe' + した (shita) 'under'.

items.english: Emma-san didn't borrow any money from Nakamura-san.
items.target: エマさんはなかむらさんにおかねをかりませんでした
items.note: Mirror of なかむらさんはエマさんにおかねをかしませんでした, the same non-event described from the other side.
